title: The segmented thumb moves by the system's own Liquid Glass morph, never out of its rail
goal: User 2026-09-29, with two screenshots of View | Edit in the title bar: 'the segmented control overshoots like CRAZY. I'm on Edit, click View, look at the crazy weird overshoot. When I click the opposite direction it does the same thing, but gets clipped. Gross and terrible. This doesn't feel mac native.' The first click threw the glass thumb far right, past the rail and into the panel toggle; the other direction clipped it at the rail's left. SegmentThumbMorph (PhotonzCore/SegmentThumbMotion.swift) is bounded to the row, so the leading theory, UNPROVEN, is a double animation: the thumb is placed per frame by a TimelineView (SegmentedControl.swift ~380) AND carries .glassEffect with .glassEffectID('thumb') in a GlassEffectContainer (~478-486), so the system also animates the glass shape with its own spring, lagging and flinging it; the rail's clip then cuts it off. Reproduce by recording real frames before fixing.
acceptance: Reproduced first: the probe (with the Screen Recording grant, while the person is away) captures 30+ real window frames across Edit to View and View to Edit, logging the drawn thumb's bounds against the rail; the report confirms or refutes the double-animation theory

The hand-rolled motion is removed: no TimelineView placement of the thumb, no SegmentThumbMorph keyframes (delete it and its tests, or keep only what the drag needs). The user chose this on 2026-09-29 after asking whether Swift gives real Liquid Glass

The system does the motion: the thumb is a real .glassEffect capsule drawn behind the selected segment, in a GlassEffectContainer with one .glassEffectID shared across the segments' slots (or a matchedGeometryEffect on a single glass capsule), and a change of selection happens inside withAnimation with the system's own smooth curve; macOS morphs it. Nothing else animates its frame

Lighter than the rail comes from the glass itself (Glass .regular with .tint, or the clear/regular variant over the recessed rail), not a gradient painted over the glass; measured thumb vs rail contrast at least 1.5:1 in light and dark, in the title bar and the panel
In every captured frame the whole thumb, glass and shadow included, stays inside the rail in both directions; no clipping needed
Drag to slide: while dragging, the glass capsule follows the pointer (the system permits a non-animated frame update during a drag), and on release withAnimation lands it on the nearest segment
Reduce Motion, Reduce Transparency and Increase Contrast still behave (system glass honours them; check)
Every use gets it (title bar View | Edit and the panel pickers); a card asks the user to judge the feel with the captured frames and a before/after

log.note: Reproduced first with a new walk step, filmThumb (SCStream of the window at 120fps, each frame read column by column through the rail). Before the fix: Edit to View drew the whole glass capsule on the panel toggle for ~50ms (frames with no glass on the rail at all), then 102pt on a 96pt rail; View to Edit pressed the glass 4pt over the rail's left padding, cut off by the rail. The Across panel picker stayed within 0.5pt. Cause: EditorState.setViewEditMode changes the mode inside withAnimation(.viewEditMode), so SwiftUI animated the thumb's placement additively on top of the TimelineView morph (old-to-new distance counted twice, the wrong way first). glassEffectID was NOT the cause (panel pickers had it too and stayed inside), but was removed anyway so the thumb has one animator.

Fix: .transaction{disablesAnimations; animation=nil} on the thumb's TimelineView; a restingOn state keeps the thumb on its old slot for the one pass before onChange starts the morph (no flash on the new slot); glassEffectID + GlassEffectContainer dropped (plain .glassEffect stays); SegmentThumbMorph now the page's 300ms two-leg curve, no settle, tests hold no-overshoot and monotonic edges. After: 0.0pt past rest in both directions, 0 frames off the rail; segmented-thumb-film-walk (inside: true on all four moves), segmented-thumb-glass-walk (real drag), segment-tooltips, view-mode-and-edit-mode, panel-toggle-titlebar all green at Next defaults; Scripts/test.sh 10536 tests green. Card for the feel is on the-segmented-thumb-moves-the-way-the-user-likes (old card withdrawn as overtaken). Left rough: View to Edit on the big fixture skips the glide's first ~100ms because the mode switch holds the main thread (folded into switching-a-long-recording-to-edit-mode-draws-it).

Reproduced on real frames with a new filmThumb walk step: the title bar picks inside withAnimation, so SwiftUI animated the thumb's placement on top of its morph (Edit to View drew the glass on the panel toggle; View to Edit pressed it 4pt past the rail's end). Fixed in DesignSystem/SegmentedControl.swift (one animator, no flash on the new slot, no glassEffectID) and PhotonzCore/SegmentThumbMotion.swift (page's 300ms curve, no overshoot, tests updated). Filmed after: 0.0pt past rest both ways, 0 frames off the rail. segmented-thumb-film-walk, segmented-thumb-glass-walk (real drag), segment-tooltips, view-mode-and-edit-mode, panel-toggle-titlebar green at Next defaults; Scripts/test.sh 10536 tests green. Audit 2026-09-29-segmented-thumb-glide; the card on the feel sits on the-segmented-thumb-moves-the-way-the-user-likes.
User 2026-09-29 chose: use the system's glass morph (glassEffectID/withAnimation), ban the hand-rolled per-frame animation; tint the glass rather than paint a gradient over it. Acceptance rewritten.
